# engineer-of-source experience — Marix

## Workflow runtime

- The active hierarchy is Task → Intent → Step → Invocation/Relay. Intent owns plain Plan state; there is no active Plan actor or protocol namespace.
- Register every child actor in its task-wide registry before `start`. On termination, commit lifecycle result/status and complete the registry entry before notifying the owner; reversing either order creates lookup races.
- `Lifecycle` stores `ActorStatus<Result>` atomically. Parent updates carry the terminal child result; use registry result lookup only for dynamic reconstruction.
- Task uses a current-thread Tokio runtime driven by a dedicated standard thread. Spawn child actors through that shared runtime; blocking the task dispatcher prevents every nested actor from progressing.
- `TaskAccess` permits construction/insertion only. Keep lookup, completion, cancellation, lineage checks, and routing in `TaskRuntime`; retain its weak `SessionContext` link.
## Model and tool boundaries

- Deepseek is stream-only. Buffer SSE tool-call fragments by index, require a valid terminal `[DONE]`, validate complete JSON-object arguments, then emit one normalized `StepDraft`; never execute partial deltas.
- 2026-07-20: DeepSeek chat-completion payloads explicitly disable Thinking in the base payload because Thinking rejects `tool_choice`; keep forced tool relays on `tool_choice: "required"` and non-tool relays on JSON response format.
- Invocation validates the exact registered tool name and JSON arguments. Return validation and unknown-tool failures through normal typed results so parent actors cannot strand.
- Windows managed processes launch executables directly with explicit arguments. Validate UUID paths, reject symlinks, bind ownership to PID plus creation time, bound output pages, and retain the lock file.
- 2026-07-21: Native web search invokes DuckDuckGo, Yahoo, and Wikipedia through curl with a 60-second per-attempt `--max-time`; preserve provider fallback order and retry settings together.
- 2026-07-22: Tool-call-summarize is a native Workflow Tool call (`workflow_call_summary`, in `protocol/workflow/call_summary.rs`), not an isolated JSON-mode relay — `RelayKind::ToolCallSummarize` is a struct variant `{ invocation: InvocationSignature, tool: String, output: String }` (sibling to the unit variant `RelayKind::IntentAnalyze`), and `RelayRuntime::model_request`/`context_prompts` in `server/relay/prompt.rs` stay a *single unconditional* code path shared by both variants; only one extra trailing prompt string differs, appended via `if let RelayKind::ToolCallSummarize { tool, output, .. } = &self.kind { prompts.push(Self::tool_call_prompt(tool, output)); }` right after `pending_intent_prompt`. This keeps the system prompt + every context-chain prompt except the last byte-identical between a normal decision call and a summarize call for the same intent state — that prefix-identity (for model-provider prompt/token-cache reuse) is the entire point of the design, so any future change to this path must preserve it rather than re-forking per-`RelayKind` request builders.
- 2026-07-27: Per-chunk tool-output summarization used to be amnesiac: `InvocationRuntime` already accumulated each chunk's summary in its private `summaries: StdMutex<Vec<String>>` (pushed in `on_summarize_update`, joined in `finish_summary`), but that list was never sent outward, so every chunk after the first was summarized with zero knowledge of what earlier chunks found. The fix threads it through `RelayKind::ToolCallSummarize.previous_summaries: Vec<String>` (`#[serde(default)]`), snapshotted in `summarize_and_finish` via `Self::lock(&self.summaries).clone()` — at that point the list holds exactly the PREVIOUS chunks, since the current chunk is only pushed after its relay returns. Reuse that one field; do not add a parallel list.
- 2026-07-27: Conditional prompt content must be carried in a parameter value, not as static template text, whenever the no-content render has to stay byte-identical. `Prompt::prompt()` rejects only `None` injections, so `Some("")` renders as nothing, and `Prompt::slice_marker` emits each `{{#name}}` as its own slice — so `{{#pre_chunk}}[TOOL: {{#tool}}]` on one line collapses to exactly `[TOOL: web_fetch]` when empty. `RelayRuntime::render_prompt` requires every template placeholder to have a supplied value but silently ignores extra supplied parameters (it iterates `prompt.parameters()`, not the supplied slice), so over-supplying is safe while under-supplying is not.
- 2026-07-27: `ExecutorCache::try_cache` returns `Ok((content, None))` once the remainder is at or below `CACHE_THRESHOLD_BYTES`, so the FINAL chunk of a continuation chain arrives with no cursor and renders through `ToolCallSummarize.prompt`, not `ToolCallSummarizeWithCursor.prompt`. Any per-chunk context added for chunked output must go into BOTH templates or the last chunk stays blind.
- 2026-07-27: Static model-facing prose belongs in `prompt/module/*.prompt`, but only the *static* part: `RelayRuntime::pre_chunk_text` keeps its `[PRE-CHUNK: {tool}]` header and `{n}. {summary}` list in Rust (variable-length data the template engine cannot express — it has no loop/conditional syntax) and loads only the trailing fixed sentence via `Self::render_prompt(module, Prompt::load_module, &[])`. Module files are CRLF-terminated on disk here, so `trim_end()` the render before re-appending the exact `"\n\n"` the Rust code used, or a third newline leaks in. A module name may mirror the template pair convention (base name plus a `WithCursor` suffix, as in `ToolCallSummarize`/`ToolCallSummarizeWithCursor`), but `PreChunk` deliberately has no `WithCursor` twin any more — see the 2026-07-27 collapse entry below; `Prompt::assert_identifier` allows only ASCII alphanumerics and underscore, so hyphens are rejected.
- 2026-07-27: Moving a Rust literal into a `.prompt` file makes the containing helper fallible; keep any early "renders nothing" return above the load so the common path stays infallible and filesystem-free. That property is provable at runtime, not just by inspection: point `MARIX_CONFIG` at a nonexistent path and confirm the empty-input call returns `Ok("")` while a non-empty call returns `Err("failed to load prompt ...: failed to load config for prompt ...")`.
- 2026-07-27: To prove a prompt-relocation refactor is byte-identical, dump the pre-change helper output to files from a throwaway `#[cfg(test)] mod` inside the same source file (private associated fns are reachable from a child module), then re-run the same dump after the change and `assert_eq!` against the saved bytes. `Prompt::load_module` needs a real config: write a full `config.toml` into a scratch root with `marix_path = "."`, `unsafe { std::env::set_var("MARIX_CONFIG", ...) }`, and mirror the real `.prompt` files into `<root>/prompt/module/`. `Config::load` caches process-globally, so run each such test as its own `cargo test ... -- --exact` invocation. Rust lib-test filters need the full module path (`relay::prompt::scratch_prechunk::name`), not the bare module name.
- 2026-07-27: Multi-line Rust string literals using trailing `\` continuations collapse to a SINGLE line — the backslash eats the newline and the next line's leading whitespace — so `"a \`<newline>`     b"` is `"a b"`, not `"a\n b"`. When relocating such a literal into a text file, dump the real runtime value first rather than transcribing the source by eye.
- 2026-07-27: `cargo clippy` fingerprints are mtime-based, so restoring files with `Copy-Item` (which preserves the source LastWriteTime) can make cargo reuse a stale rlib and report a phantom `E0559 ... has no field` against source that clearly has the field. When doing a stash-free A/B baseline by copying files back and forth, reset `LastWriteTime` to now afterwards and confirm the run actually printed `Checking <crate>` lines before trusting the comparison.
- 2026-07-27: `cargo fmt --check` is NOT clean at baseline in `marix-server`/`marix-protocol` — the codebase deliberately hand-wraps near 70 columns while rustfmt targets 100, so dozens of pre-existing diffs exist. Do not run `cargo fmt` to "fix" a touched file; match the surrounding hand-wrapped style instead, or the formatter will rewrite unrelated code.
- 2026-07-27: Prompt templates under `src/server/prompt/template/` are CRLF in the worktree while every Rust-built prompt fragment (`pending_intent_prompt`, `plan_prompt`, `pre_chunk_text`) uses `\n`. Keep `\n` in Rust — hardcoding `\r\n` would be wrong on Linux deployments — and accept the mixed endings inside a rendered message.
- 2026-07-22: `IntentRuntime::verdict()` (`server/intent/runtime.rs`) and the analogous `InvocationRuntime::render_workflow_policy()` (`server/invocation/runtime.rs`) both hardcode the literal string `"WorkflowPolicy"` three times (in `Prompt::load(...)`, the panic-detail format, and two more error messages) rather than factoring it into a local `template` variable — unlike `RelayRuntime::system_prompt`'s style in `server/relay/prompt.rs`, which does use a local `let template = "System";`. When adding a third `Prompt::load` call site for the same template name, match whichever sibling call site is closer in shape/intent rather than assuming one style is universal across the codebase.
- 2026-07-21: A model backend can be fully self-contained (e.g. `src/server/model/glm/`): own its own `XConfig` struct inside `backend.rs` instead of `common/config`, take it directly in `new(config)`, and stay unreferenced except for the two mirrored lines in `model/mod.rs` (`pub mod x;` / `pub use x::XBackend;`). A `pub use`-exported but never-constructed backend does not trigger a dead-code warning under `cargo check`, so an intentionally-unwired sibling backend compiles clean without `#[allow(dead_code)]`. GLM's chat-completions API is OpenAI-compatible SSE, so its stream accumulator mirrors Deepseek's byte-for-byte (same five-tool-call cap, same `stop`/`tool_calls` finish_reason values, same `thinking: {"type":"disabled"}` payload field).
- 2026-07-21: Deepseek's and Glm's near-duplicate stream/request/payload logic was consolidated into `src/server/model/openai.rs` (`pub(super) struct OpenAiCore`, sibling-scoped so `deepseek`/`glm` submodules can use it but nothing outside `model` can). Each backend now holds `core: OpenAiCore` and delegates `ModelBackendImpl`/`Debug`. Provider-specific text (log/error strings) is threaded through a `provider: &'static str` field/param instead of being hardcoded per backend — this is the general pattern for extracting shared logic behind a `pub(super)` core type when two+ sibling modules are byte-for-byte identical except for one label.
- 2026-07-23: Every `src/tool/native/*` binary is a one-shot OS process per `tool_main.rs`: reads one JSON payload from stdin, prints one JSON result, exits — no persisted state, no task/session id passed in (confirmed via `src/host/executor/tool.rs`, which spawns each tool with bare stdin/stdout/stderr pipes only). Any "remember more than fits" feature (pagination, continuation) for these tools must therefore be stateless re-fetch/re-request-and-reslice on every call, matching the existing internal convention in `tool/native/process/output.rs` (`OutputSnapshot::from_path`: structured `offset`/`max_bytes` in, `next_offset`/`truncated` out, `offset > length` errors, `offset == length` is a valid empty read) — never a disk cache, and never a natural-language "call again with X" hint embedded in the content string.
- 2026-07-23: `web_fetch.rs` and `web_search.rs` (`src/tool/native/web/`) intentionally use two different error-helper styles that must each be preserved on their own file: `web_fetch.rs`'s `failure()` is a free module function (not `Self::`), so its own size-limit consts (`DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH`/`MAX_MAX_LENGTH`) were added as free top-level `const`s (not inside `impl WebFetch`) specifically so error messages can use plain inline format captures like `{MAX_MAX_LENGTH}`; `web_search.rs`'s `failure()` is `Self::failure` and its `MAX_RESULTS` lives inside `impl WebSearch`, so its analogous message must use a non-inlined positional arg (`"...to {}", Self::MAX_RESULTS`) since `Self::X` path expressions cannot be inlined in a format string. Match whichever style a given file already uses rather than normalizing both to one convention.
- 2026-07-23: Wikipedia's `opensearch` API (`search_wikipedia` in `web_search.rs`) is prefix/relevance search, not count-based pagination — it has no `offset`/`s`/`b`-style parameter and always searches from the top regardless of caller-requested offset. When threading an `offset` through `WebSearch::search`'s provider fallback chain (DuckDuckGo → Yahoo → Wikipedia), only the first two providers gained the parameter; Wikipedia's call signature and behavior stayed untouched as a deliberate, documented limitation, not an oversight.
- 2026-07-23: Tool-output continuation is a Host platform concern, not native-tool pagination: `host/execution/runtime.rs` passes completed ordinary output through the process-global cache in `host/executor/output_cache.rs`, while `host/executor/runtime.rs` intercepts `workflow_continuation` before registry lookup and serves one cached page through normal Invocation events. Cache entries are FIFO (10), task-owned, and byte-offset cursors never reach Tool EXEs.
- 2026-07-23: `host/executor/cache.rs::ExecutorCache` supersedes the task-owned offset design above: it stores only content plus opaque UUID cursors, consumes an entry on every `pick`, and re-caches only the remainder after a UTF-8-safe 16 KiB chunk. `host/execution/runtime.rs` leaves short ordinary output uncached and locks the shared `ExecutorState` cache only after Tool execution; `host/executor/runtime.rs` uses the same cache for `workflow_continuation`.
- 2026-07-27: `ExecutorCache::generate_cursor`'s `tc_` cursor is a short-lived, in-memory-only opaque key compared solely by plain string equality in `remove_entry`, capped at `CACHE_CAPACITY = 10` entries — no other module or test in the workspace assumes any particular cursor length/format, so shortening it (32 hex chars → 8) was a pure `generate_cursor`-local change with zero ripple. `ToolCallSummarize[ByCursor].prompt` fence tool output in a Markdown triple-backtick block instead of a `Result:` label line (`RelayRuntime::tool_call_prompt` in `server/relay/prompt.rs` just substitutes `{{#tool}}`/`{{#output}}`/`{{#continuation_cursor}}` into the template text verbatim, so static wording/formatting inside the `.prompt` file is free to change without touching Rust); the cursor variant's own label became the bracketed `[CONTINUATION CURSOR] {{#continuation_cursor}}` tag to match the family's existing `[TOOL CALL]`/`[TOOL: ...]`/`[CURRENT TASK]` bracketed-tag convention.

## Rust language gotchas hit during refactors

- When a private helper takes two-or-more reference-shaped parameters (e.g. `provider: &str` plus `value: Option<&serde_json::Value>`) and its return type borrows from only one of them, elision fails with E0106 ("missing lifetime specifier") because 2+ input lifetimes make the borrow source ambiguous. Fix by naming an explicit lifetime tied only to the parameter actually borrowed from, e.g. `fn f<'a>(provider: &str, value: Option<&'a Value>) -> Option<&'a [Value]>` — leave the unrelated parameter's lifetime elided/independent.
- If a `#[derive(Clone)]` struct gains a field whose type does not itself derive `Clone`, the derive fails at the *call site* (`Backend: Clone` bound not satisfied), not at the field's own definition — when wrapping shared state (e.g. `OpenAiCore`) inside multiple `Clone`-deriving wrapper structs, add `#[derive(Clone)]` to the shared type itself. `reqwest::Client` is `Arc`-backed internally, so cloning it is cheap and safe to do per-request/per-task.
- Clippy's `too_many_arguments` (default threshold 7) can appear as a *new* warning purely from splitting one bundled config struct into N free function parameters during a refactor, even when total information carried is unchanged. Prefer cloning the owning struct (`self.clone()`) into a single owned local and passing that one value into the spawned task/helper, over decomposing it into many scalar parameters — this is usually also a more faithful read of "use `self.field`"-style refactor instructions.
- The Rust coding style doc's ~500-line soft-file-size guideline can be explicitly overridden by an explicit task instruction to consolidate into "a single file, not a subdirectory" — when the two conflict, the explicit, more specific instruction wins; note the override rather than silently splitting the file back up.
- 2026-07-21: On this workspace's cargo version, `cargo fmt --check --workspace` errors ("unexpected argument '--workspace'" — it wants workspace args after `--`); use `cargo fmt --all --check` instead to format-check every workspace member.
- 2026-07-22: `clippy::large_enum_variant` (default ~200-byte threshold) can newly trigger purely from reshaping a variant from a tuple with one `InvocationSignature` field into a struct variant adding two more `String` fields — before concluding a clippy warning is "newly introduced by this change" rather than pre-existing, do a controlled A/B: temporarily swap back to the old shape, re-run clippy scoped to just the affected crate, and confirm the warning disappears. This codebase already carries several pre-existing, unaddressed instances of the same lint elsewhere (e.g. `SessionEvent` in `protocol/session/event.rs`, `StepEvent` in `protocol/step/event.rs`) without boxing large fields, so treat `large_enum_variant` as an accepted/tolerated lint class here — don't silently "fix" it by boxing fields when the enum shape itself was explicitly spec'd verbatim by the task.
- 2026-07-22: After swapping a file's content out-of-band via PowerShell (`Set-Content`/`Move-Item`) for a throwaway A/B clippy test and then restoring the original bytes, `cargo check`/`clippy` can report a suspiciously-fast "Finished" (around 1s) without actually recompiling the crate — Cargo's fingerprint check can fail to observe a real mtime change across the round-trip swap, so it silently reuses a stale cached artifact reflecting the *intermediate* (wrong) content, and the *next* `cargo check`/`clippy` invocation then surfaces spurious compile errors against what is actually correct, restored source. Fix: after any out-of-band file-swap test, force `(Get-Item path).LastWriteTime = Get-Date` and/or `cargo clean -p <pkg>` before trusting the next `cargo check`/`clippy` run — a single suspiciously-instant "Finished" is not proof of a genuine clean recompile.
- 2026-07-21: A "discriminator + N mandatory payload sections" config shape (e.g. `selected: String` plus always-required `deepseek: DeepseekConfig, glm: GlmConfig`) is strictly simpler to deserialize than a data-carrying enum: every section is a plain non-`Option` field, so a missing section surfaces for free as serde's own "missing field" error (bucketed under the existing `ConfigError::Toml` variant) — no custom `ConfigError` variant or manual validation needed. When replacing a data-carrying enum with this shape, `RawXxxx` intermediate-deserialization structs typically become unnecessary too: derive `Deserialize` directly on the real public struct, and reserve `#[serde(default = "...")]`/`#[serde(skip, default = "...")]` only for the few fields that are genuinely optional-with-a-computed-default (e.g. `core: CoreConfig` via `#[serde(default = "default_core_config")]`, `system: System` via `#[serde(skip, default = "System::new")]`) or need post-`toml::from_str` path resolution (e.g. `runtime`, `tool.directory`) — `build_config` then collapses to one `toml::from_str` call plus a couple of targeted field mutations, not a full manual struct reconstruction.
- 2026-07-21: A `grep` pattern using a long `|`-alternation group inside a quoted-string literal match (e.g. `"name": "(Config|RuntimeConfig|...|CONFIG_FILE)"` with 10+ alternatives) can return zero matches even though the content is present and a simpler single-term grep for one of the same alternatives succeeds immediately after — root cause not fully diagnosed (possibly an alternation-count limit or literal-parenthesis/quote escaping interaction). Workaround: prefer short, simple patterns (2-4 alternatives, or one distinctive substring) over long enumerated alternations when grepping JSON/text metadata.
- 2026-07-21: When a chain of two uncommitted tasks does "design A landed, then a follow-up task fully undoes/replaces design A with design B" without an intervening commit, `git diff` against the last real commit shows only the *net* structural delta — any type/field that was added by the first task and removed by the second never appears in the diff at all (as if it never existed). This is a good sanity check for design-metadata status decisions: if a `design.json` element was marked `added` (not `modified`/`renamed`) because "no prior evidence of it existing," a clean `git diff` against HEAD showing that same identifier as a fresh `+` addition (with no corresponding `-` removal of a same-named-but-different-shaped prior version) corroborates the call.
- 2026-07-24: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` is NOT clean on this workspace's committed baseline (pre-existing debt, unrelated to any one change) — it fails on a dozen-ish distinct lint violations spread across `marix-common` (`module_inception`, `new_without_default`, `derivable_impls`, `while_let_on_iterator`, `type_complexity`, `too_many_arguments`, in files like `actor/mod.rs`, `actor/lifecycle.rs`, `config/sys.rs`, `logging/source.rs`, `logging/store/*.rs`, and `structure/channel.rs`'s own pre-existing `accept_loop`/`connect_attempt` `setup_tx` parameter type) and `marix-host` (`module_inception` in `execution/mod.rs`/`executor/mod.rs`, `new_without_default` for `ToolRegistry`). Plain `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features` (no `-D warnings`) does exit 0 today and matches the coding-style doc's actual documented invocation — treat that as the real clean gate for this repo. To audit whether a specific change introduces *new* findings under the stricter flag, do a git-stash-based A/B: stash your own diff, rerun `-D warnings` on the pristine baseline, compare the error sets, then restore your stash — don't assume `-D warnings` itself must pass.
- 2026-07-27: This workspace's vendored `uuid` 1.23.4 (`uuid::fmt::{Simple,Hyphenated,Urn,Braced}`, reached via `marix_common::external::uuid`) implements `Display`/`LowerHex` by calling `f.write_str(self.encode_lower(...))` directly (see its `impl_fmt_traits!` macro), never `f.pad(...)` — so a width/precision format spec like `format!("{:.8}", uuid.simple())` silently ignores the `.8` and still prints the full 32-hex-char string (confirmed empirically: produced a 35-char `tc_`+32-hex result, not 8). This is general Rust behavior, not uuid-specific: any custom `Display` impl that skips `Formatter::pad` ignores precision/width/fill/align entirely. To truncate such a value, slice its `.to_string()` explicitly, e.g. `format!("tc_{}", &uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string()[..8])` — verified this yields exactly `tc_` + 8 lowercase hex chars. When a task's suggested `{:.N}` snippet and an "if that doesn't work, use this slice instead" fallback are both given, empirically probe with a throwaway `#[test]` (delete it afterward) rather than assuming the first form compiles-and-truncates correctly.

## Transport and configuration

- Remoc setup must keep its connection future driven after returning channels. Abort guarded connection tasks on timeout/rejection; otherwise failed handshakes leak workers.
- Server channel listeners bind the IPv4 wildcard independently of `server.ip`; connectors resolve the configured address. Server-driven host registration sends session identity and tool query before publishing the channel.
- Install a remote telemetry sink only after TCP, remoc, and token acceptance succeed. Startup telemetry exhaustion is fatal rather than a silent local fallback.
- 2026-07-24: `connect_channel<T>(endpoint)` in `structure/channel.rs` is a 1-line wrapper (`connect_channel_with_timeout(endpoint, CONNECT_TIMEOUT)`) around the real logic, which now lives in `pub fn connect_channel_with_timeout<T>(endpoint, timeout: Duration)` — this is the general pattern for giving one caller (here, Host) a different timeout/no-retry variant while every existing caller (Client, `Logger::connect_sender`'s 5-attempt retry loop, ~10 sites in `structure/tests/channel.rs`) keeps calling the original 1-arg function with zero call-site changes and byte-identical behavior. `Logger` mirrors this with `connect(source, timeout)` beside the untouched, still-5-attempt-retrying `connect_with_retry(source)` (renamed 2026-07-24 from `connect_once`/`connect` respectively, to resolve the naming ambiguity, pure rename with zero behavior change): both funnel through the same generic private `remote_sink(fallback_path, connect_sender: impl FnOnce() -> Result<NetSender<LogMessage>, LoggingError>)` helper, so `connect` only needed to supply a different one-shot closure (`connect_channel_with_timeout(..., timeout).map(...)`) — `connect_with_retry()`'s own `connect_sender()` (`MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5`, `RETRY_BACKOFF = 200ms`) was not touched.
- 2026-07-24: A bare `panic!()` inside a `std::thread::spawn`-ed worker thread does NOT terminate the OS process if the main thread's own loop ignores join results — confirmed in `host/main.rs`, whose main thread runs `session.run(); loop { std::thread::park(); }` after `HostSession::run` spawns the actual connect/worker thread, so a panicking worker would die silently while main parks forever (process alive-but-dead from outside). This is why Host's connect-failure and lost-connection paths in `host/session.rs::spawn_worker` call `std::process::exit(1)` explicitly instead of panicking: `process::exit` unconditionally kills the whole process from any thread, while a plain `panic!` only unwinds the thread that called it (this workspace's bins don't set `panic = "abort"`). Any future "this failure must kill the whole Host process" requirement inside a spawned thread must use `std::process::exit`, never rely on propagating a panic.

## Repository invariants

- Keep public protocol re-exports synchronized between `protocol/lib.rs` and its mirrored `protocol/mod.rs`.

## Logging and telemetry

- 2026-07-22: Logging severity is `LogLevel` ordered by declaration as `Debug < Info < Warning < Error`; telemetry queries treat `level` as a minimum and storage verifies `message.level >= query.level`.
- 2026-07-22: Telemetry redb schema v5 owns `telemetry_session_level_emit`, deletes the legacy exact-level index during transactional rebuild, and reads old primary JSON through `#[serde(alias = "tag")]` while all new serialization emits only `level`.
- 2026-07-22: `LogMessage.tags: Vec<String>` (`#[serde(default)]`, schema v6) is deduplicated in first-seen order via `LogMessage::dedup_tags` at construction time (`LogMessage::new`) — a single message's own tag list is NOT sorted. This is deliberately different from `Store::tags(session_id)`'s session-wide distinct-tag listing, which returns an alphabetically-sorted `Vec<String>` via `BTreeSet`. Don't conflate the two ordering conventions when touching either.
- 2026-07-22: Pattern for adding an opt-in parameter to heavily-called public methods without touching their signature (used for `Logger::log/warning/error/debug`, hundreds of existing call sites across the workspace): add sibling `_tagged` methods (`log_tagged`/`warning_tagged`/`error_tagged`/`debug_tagged`, each taking `tags: impl IntoIterator<Item = impl Into<String>>`) and thread the new data through the shared private impl only — `emit`/`telemetry` both grew a `tags: Vec<String>` parameter, with the original 4 public methods passing `Vec::new()` and the new 4 passing `Self::collect_tags(tags)`. Every existing call site keeps compiling untouched.
- 2026-07-22: New `SESSION_TAG_TABLE` redb table (`src/common/logging/store/schema.rs`) is keyed by `session_tag_key(session_id, tag) = session_key(session_id) ++ tag.as_bytes()`, one empty (`b""`) valued row per distinct (session, tag) pair, populated inside `index_message` (shared by `record_batch` and `rebuild_indexes`) via `for tag in &message.tags`. `Store::tags(session_id)` (new `store/tags.rs`) range-scans just that session's key prefix, strips the prefix to recover each tag string, and collects into a `BTreeSet<String>` for free dedup+sort — this needed a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (5→6) so `ensure_schema()`'s `required`-table check forces old stores to `rebuild_indexes()` and backfill it. By contrast, tag *filtering* needed neither a new table nor a schema bump: `Store::matches(message, query, keyword)` in `reader.rs` just grew one more `&&`-chained OR-check (`query.tags.is_empty() || query.tags.iter().any(|tag| message.tags.contains(tag))`) appended after the existing level/keyword checks — since every scan path (`index_range_records`, `trigram_index_records`, `session_incremental_records`) already funnels through this one shared predicate, the new filter applies everywhere from a single edit site.
- 2026-07-22: `Logger::log_tagged`/`error_tagged` call sites take their tag list as an array literal (`["Model Relay"]`); growing it to N tags is a pure literal edit (`["Model Relay", "Request"]`) with zero syntax adjustment needed — a `[&'static str; N]` array satisfies `tags: impl IntoIterator<Item = impl Into<String>>` for any N, confirmed in `src/server/model/openai.rs`'s 4 call sites (moving `[Request]`/`[Response]` out of the message-text bracket and into a second tag, while `[{task_id}]` stayed in the text since task IDs are unbounded-cardinality and unsuited to the low-cardinality Tags dropdown).
- 2026-07-22: After a text-only shortening edit to a `Logger::*_tagged` call's `format!(...)` message argument, `cargo fmt` can leave one call site inline but reflow a **textually near-identical sibling** call site (same arg shapes/arity, similar string lengths, well under the 100-char `max_width`) into 4-line block form instead — the split is not simply "does the single-line version exceed max_width" (verified by measuring the hypothetical single-line reconstruction at 90 chars, under 100, and even reproducing a minimal standalone `rustfmt` snippet with the same shape that stayed inline). ## Design-metadata (`src_meta/`) nuances

- 2026-07-21: `pub(super)` counts as "outward-facing" for `design-json-update` element-tracking purposes, same as `pub`/`pub(crate)`/`pub(in ...)` — a `pub(super) fn` gets its own tracked element even though it never appears in the crate's genuine public API surface.

Reserve `renamed`/rename-in-place strictly for identifiers that already had their own tracked element under the old name.
- 2026-07-21: `src/common/structure/tests/channel.rs` (any path under a `tests/` folder, at any depth) gets zero design.json treatment — it is not scanned for elements and its changes never appear in any folder's status arrays, confirmed via both the `changed`- and `full`-mode path rules.

When a change touches a deeply-nested file, always check the immediate-parent design.json's *existing* convention for that specific child (does it mirror elements at all? functions too, or just structs/enums?) rather than assuming one of the three patterns — do not try to harmonize them, per the skill's own explicit warning that conventions are inconsistent.

- 2026-07-22: **Validation-checklist blind spot**: the skill's own Validation steps catch only *structural* problems (JSON parses, required fields present, ranges in-bounds) — they cannot catch a codeSegment that's simply missing `modifiedLines` for a real change. - 2026-07-27: Telemetry Portal dropdowns had TWO independent "closes/breaks while logs stream" causes, both proven with headless Chrome against the real assets. (1) `createDropdown`'s `window.addEventListener("scroll", close, true)` is CAPTURE phase, so it observes scrolls of ANY element even though scroll does not bubble; `requestLogs("incremental")` -> `scrollToBottom(logAreaEl)` fires a `#log-area` scroll every 2s and closed BOTH Level and Tags. Fix: close only when `_event.target.contains(_button)` (page/document scrolls still close; `#log-area` and the popup's own overflow list no longer do). (2) `renderTagsPopup` unconditionally `replaceChildren`-ed the Tags popup on every refresh, destroying the node under the pointer/focus. Fix: split into guarded `renderTagsPopup` (defers via `_tagsRenderPending` while `isOpen()`, still updates the button label) and unguarded `renderTagsPopupContent`; `createDropdown` gained an optional `_onOpen` invoked after `_open = true` but BEFORE `position()`, so the deferred rebuild is measured with fresh content. The open-time callback must call the UNGUARDED function -- calling the guarded one deadlocks (`_open` is already true, so it re-defers forever and the new content never appears). `toggleTag` must not rebuild either; it now patches only the clicked `<li>`'s `selected` class / `aria-selected` plus the button label.
- 2026-07-27: `src/server_telemetry/http` has no build step, so verify it by serving the real files from a scratch Node stub that mirrors `router.rs` route names (`/` -> page.html, `/telemetry.css` -> page.css, `/telemetry-*.js`, `/api/sessions`, `/api/sessions/{id}/tags`, `/api/logs`) and driving it with puppeteer installed OUTSIDE the repo under `%TEMP%`. `/api/logs` must return fresh items on every `after_id` poll to reach the `loadAvailableTags` branch at the end of `requestLogs`. Prove node identity with a JS expando (`li.__probe`) -- it survives in-place attribute edits and dies on `replaceChildren` -- and prove causality with a capture-phase scroll tracer plus MutationObservers on the popup's `hidden` attribute and `childList`.

- 2026-07-27: Telemetry Portal log rows dropped the right-click context menu: left click -> `openMessage(_summary, _row)` (format modal), right click -> `copyMessage(_event, _summary)` (`preventDefault` + clipboard + toast). Chrome fires NO `click` event for the secondary button (only `contextmenu`/`auxclick`), proven in headless Chrome with a capture-phase `click` recorder that stayed empty across a real `button:'right'` press -- so an `_event.button === 0` guard in the click handler would be dead code. Likewise, `inert` on `#app` plus the `position:fixed; inset:0` backdrop already make row clicks impossible while the modal is open (real mouse click at row coordinates produced one `click` whose target was the backdrop DIV, never a `#log-body` row), so `openMessage` needs no `_modalOpen` re-entry guard; the removed `openContextMenu` guard was not load-bearing. `_modalPreviousFocus` semantics are unchanged by moving capture to click time: `mousedown` on a non-focusable `<tr>` blurs any focused input first, so `document.activeElement` is `<body>` in both the old contextmenu handler and the new click handler. Deleting the menu also retired `bindAction` (its only two callers), the `pointerdown` outside-click handler, and the `scroll`(capture)/`resize` dismissal handlers; note `telemetry-dropdown.js`'s header comment still cites `openContextMenu/closeContextMenu` as its model and is now stale.

- 2026-07-27: Telemetry Portal log rows got their click affordance: `cursor: pointer` on `tbody tr.log-row` in `page.css`, plus a real hover lift. The `tbody tr.log-row:hover, tbody tr.log-row:focus-within { background: var(--task-background-hover); }` rule and the `--task-background-hover` custom property had existed all along, but `taskRowColors` returned `hoverColor === color` on BOTH branches (hashed and the null/no-task `#000` fallback), so the rule swapped a colour for itself and hovering repainted nothing. Proven in headless Chrome before the fix: `row.matches(":hover")` was `true` while `getComputedStyle(row).backgroundColor` per-channel delta was `[0,0,0]` on all four sampled rows -- the `:hover` state engaged, the value was just identical, so any test asserting only "the hover rule exists" or ":hover matched" would have passed against the bug. Assert the rendered `backgroundColor` differs across a real `page.mouse.move`. Fix is a flat additive `c_rowHoverLift = 12` applied uniformly to all three channels through `liftChannel`/`hoverColorFrom(_channels)`, which the null branch also calls as `hoverColorFrom([0, 0, 0])`; a uniform additive lift preserves each task's hue relationship, whereas a multiplicative one would leave near-zero channels dead. Base channels are tiny (`_hash % 4`, `8 + (%7)`, `16 + (%9)`), so 12 is clearly visible yet is only one third of the existing `#session-list li:hover` grey (`#242424` = 36) -- faint, not a selection bar. To keep the base palette byte-identical while reusing the permuted channels for the lift, hoist them into `var _ordered = [...]` first and build `_color` from `_ordered` with the same `", "` separators. No transitions: every existing hover in `page.css` (`#session-list li:hover`, `.dropdown-popup li:hover`, toolbar border-colour hovers) repaints instantly.

- 2026-07-27: `:focus-within` parity on a `<tr>` with no focusable descendants is testable without touching production markup: set `row.tabIndex = 0`, `row.focus()`, read `getComputedStyle(row).backgroundColor`, then `blur()` and `removeAttribute("tabindex")`. `:focus-within` matches the element itself, so this exercises the real CSS rule. Move the mouse away first and assert `row.matches(":hover") === false`, otherwise hover is what you are measuring.
